speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development of the cases prosecuted for the illegal import and export of endangered species in the past five years, how many involved (i) the person prosecuted is only delivering the endangered species and is not the seller and (ii) the person prosecuted is the seller of the endangered species.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think that is the worry on the ground, that we are only catching the runners and not making an effective dent on the illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask the Minister of State whether NParks is looking into the money trail, doing financial audits for each of the wildlife crime cases that we are handling?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have not received any information from INTERPOL or our foreign enforcement agency counterparts that these persons were acting as part of a larger organised crime syndicate or network.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In response to the Member's second question, I would also like to refer the Member to the reply to his Oral Question in the Sitting on 2 November 2020, where Mr Ong Ye Kung replied on behalf of Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam, Senior Minister and Minister in-charge of MAS.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In the reply, Minister Ong Ye Kung gave a fuller reply around the various rules and regulations in place to look at illegal wildlife trade and money laundering and organised crimes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But I would just also direct the Member's attention to the part of the reply, which I think addresses his question, about having public-private partnerships playing an important role in our effort to combat illegal wildlife trade and money laundering.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Notwithstanding that, we will continue to be vigilant to the threat posed by illegal wildlife trade and related money laundering.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks will work closely with other agencies, like MAS and the other enforcement agencies, in this regard.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the orders of the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), Written Answers to Question Nos 9 and 10 on the Order Paper are reproduced in the Appendix.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The remaining Questions have been postponed to a later Sitting of Parliament or withdrawn.]
